acrobatics:
Tumbling, horizontal dives, rolling, swinging on objects, balance and general gymnastic maneuvers. If beauty is the goal, a Performance Art skill may be more appropriate.
Controlling a fall: any critical from the fall is +1 severity on Absolute Failure, -1 severity on Success, -2 severities on Absolute Success.
Difficulty depends on amount of movement and timing; rotations and somersaults make it harder.
Time Required: usually part of movement, no extra time. If the movement requires Walk or faster pace, apply pace penalties.
Specializations: none required. Optional: specific gymnastic events (parallel bars, uneven bars, etc.), use of chandeliers, curtains, whips, etc.
Alternate Usage: may replace any movement skill (e.g. Running) for Dodging; no roll needed.
acting:
Feigning emotions; using voice and body language to create a persona (original or mimicry); some ability to interpret a text or performance in terms of character motivation.
The more complex or fantastic the persona, the harder. Success = convincing portrayal (may yield only a laugh or a tear, depending on difficulty). Removing a specific component of one's demeanor is relatively simple; a believable character with idiosyncrasies and intricate emotions is much harder. Humor is easier (plausibility is not a factor).
To fool a target: conflicting maneuver vs the target's Social Awareness.
Can convey concepts non-verbally (mime, charades).
Time Required: variable, typically the duration of the interactions. A new complex character (Hard or harder) needs at least 1 hour of study and rehearsal beforehand.
Specializations: none required. Optional: Mimicry/Ventriloquism, Storytelling, a specific form of theater, a particular demeanor or character.
Complementary Skills: to deceive, Acting and Duping are complementary. Portraying an individual of a profession: an appropriate Vocation is complementary. To portray a generic member of that Vocation, may use the Vocation skill instead with Acting as complementary.
administration:
Vocations of managing, administration and organizing: procedures and practices of the vocation, managing and using records, plus some knowledge of the practices of those managed or served (a Quartermaster knows some military procedure; a Librarian knows how scholars use libraries).
Other skills may be complementary (e.g. Mathematics for Bookkeeper; Trading for Quartermaster or vice versa).
Depending on the vocation, may be used to influence operations/procedures toward a goal (e.g. which merchants are selected as suppliers). At minimum identifies which individuals must be persuaded, even if other methods (e.g. Influence) are required.
Vocation skills are a catch-all for an occupation's minor skills, not a replacement for several other skills. Also useful when impersonating or persuading a member of the occupation.
Time Required: highly variable; influencing a major decision may require sustained effort over a week or more.
Specializations: Bookkeeper, Judge, Librarian, Officer, Manager, Quartermaster, Seneschal, etc.
adrenal-defense:
Integrates dodging into natural movement. Success: partial dodging as an instantaneous action (0 AP), or full dodging with concentration. Absolute Success (double benefit): full dodging as an instantaneous action during the first round. Absolute Failure: unable to dodge at all the following round (in addition to the table result).
Use: concentrate one round, then make an absolute maneuver. On success, benefits apply the following 2 rounds, plus 2 more rounds per full 20 the maneuver succeeded by (2 rounds on 101-120, 4 on 121-140). This duration is double that of the other Adrenal skills. Absolute Success doubles the benefit for the first round.
May prepare one adrenal maneuver while using another, or use double concentration (Core Law section 8.1) to prepare two at once.
Difficulty is based on how vital the situation is and how motivated the character is (desperate defense of loved ones may be Easy (+20); a casual barroom brawl over an insult may be Very Hard (-20)).
Time Required: concentration for one round of preparation; none during use (the Dodging maneuver has its own time).
Specializations: none required. Optional: sparring in a particular competition, fighting a particular type of foe with a distinctive style.
Restricting Dodging: see the optional rule under Running.
adrenal-focus:
Success: +25 the following round to any Brawn, Gymnastic or Movement maneuver.
Use: concentrate one round, then an absolute maneuver. Benefits the following round, +1 round per full 20 succeeded by (1 round on 101-120, 2 on 121-140). Absolute Success doubles the benefit for the first round (+50).
May prepare one adrenal maneuver while using another, or prepare two at once with double concentration (Core Law section 8.1).
Difficulty: how vital the situation and how motivated the character is.
Also used to control the Frenzy talent (Core Law; see the talent). Entering a frenzy is easiest when angry, hardest when calm.
Time Required: concentration for one round of preparation; none during use (the boosted maneuver has its own time).
Specializations: none required. Optional: a specific skill to be boosted (e.g. Fortitude, Acrobatics).
adrenal-speed:
Success: +2 Action Points for the following round. Absolute Failure: loses his first 2 AP the following round.
Use: concentrate one round, then an absolute maneuver. Benefits the following round, +1 round per full 20 succeeded by (1 round on 101-120, 2 on 121-140). Absolute Success doubles the benefit for the first round (+4 AP).
May prepare one adrenal maneuver while using another, or two at once with double concentration (Core Law section 8.1).
Difficulty: as Adrenal Defense (desperate: Easy (+20); casual brawl: Very Hard (-20)).
Time Required: concentration for one round of preparation; none during use.
Specializations: none required. Optional: a single specific activity (archery, a particular sport or competition), but not the general "melee combat".
adrenal-strength:
Success: attacks treated as one size larger; character's weight treated as x4 for feats of strength. Partial Success: no effect. Absolute Failure: -1 attack size for the following round (in addition to the table result) and weight treated as 1/4 for feats of strength.
Use: concentrate one round, then an absolute maneuver. Benefits the following round, +1 round per full 20 succeeded by (1 round on 101-120, 2 on 121-140). Absolute Success doubles the benefit for the first round (attacks two sizes larger, weight x8).
May prepare one adrenal maneuver while using another, or two at once with double concentration (Core Law section 8.1).
Difficulty: as Adrenal Defense.
Time Required: concentration for one round of preparation; none during use.
Specializations: none required. Optional: sparring in a particular competition, a particular sport or athletic event.
ambush:
Very precise attack, only when the opponent is completely unaware of the attack. Attack roll as normal (with surprise bonus and often rear/flank). If a critical is obtained, the critical roll may be adjusted up or down by any number up to the character's Ambush ranks. No separate Ambush maneuver is required.
Against a foe already in melee who is unaware of the attack: Ambush ranks are halved.
Silent kill: if the target is killed or knocked unconscious, an Absolute Maneuver with Ambush makes the attack and target silent (unless the GM rules the attack cannot be silent). Difficulty depends on loudness of the attack, proximity of observers, ambient noise, noisy armor and the surface the target falls on.
Time Required: modifies an attack action; no time or action of its own.
Specializations: each Combat Training skill (e.g. Melee Weapons, Ranged Weapons) or a Directed Spells specialization (e.g. Bolts).
animal-handling:
Care, feeding, training, minor healing and possibly simple communication (depending on the animal): calming or working up animals, herding, guiding a horse, teaching tricks.
Used instead of Leadership for Fear Resistance Rolls and rallying frightened animals (Core Law Section 14.3).
May treat minor injuries on its own, or be complementary to Medicine when treating an animal's injuries or sickness.
Care: any (non-herd) domestic animal not cared for properly at least once a week has a 2% cumulative chance per week of a malady (-1d10 to each stat), assuming ready food and water. One successful maneuver per week (one attempt per day) prevents penalties. A failure causes no damage but annoys the creature (-10 to all maneuvers with it for 24 hours). Absolute Failure may injure the animal.
Time Required: simple order to a well-trained animal: free action. Complex order or one against instinct: 0-2 AP. Communicating an idea or influencing a wild animal: 2-4 AP. Training: 1 hour/day for one week (Easy, Light, Medium tasks), two weeks (Hard, Very Hard), one month (more difficult).
Specializations: each specific type of animal.
arcane-spell-list:
Ranks in a list = the level up to which the character can cast from it (e.g. 8 ranks in Fire Law: any spell up to 8th level, though spells above his own level may be difficult).
Ranks plus realm stat (once) are added to the Spellcasting Roll.
The full skill bonus is used for Spell Mastery: changing the spell as it is cast (e.g. smaller Fire Ball, shaping a Wall of Fire). Other uses specified in certain spells. The difficulties below are for Spell Mastery. Casting modifiers: see Spell Law.
Five Spell List skills, each list a specialization:
• Base: the specialized lists of each magic-using profession.
• Open: common, straightforward spells understood by anyone of the realm.
• Closed: more esoteric techniques, understood by any user of the realm but with greater difficulty.
• Arcane: obscure or exotic magics outside the three realms.
• Restricted: any list the GM allows that is not Base, Open, Closed or Arcane (e.g. another profession's Base list).
Lists from realms other than your own cannot be developed.
Time Required: spellcasting (including spell mastery) 2-4 AP, optionally concentration for each round of preparation. Instant spells: 0 AP (instantaneous actions).
Specializations: each Base, Open, Closed, Arcane or Restricted Spell List.
architecture:
Science of building construction (specialized engineering plus artistic training). Needed to plan large/complicated enduring structures or new designs; includes large-scale traps and built-in mechanisms (e.g. elevators).
Can determine weak points of large structures, distinguish load-bearing walls (vs those that might conceal portals), identify voids that might be hidden chambers, predict which part of a building serves a function.
Time Required: from 2-4 AP (identifying a style) to many weeks (designing complex structures). Insight into construction/layout: at least 1 minute for a single room (e.g. locating a hidden portal), 10 minutes for a larger area.
Specializations: none required. Optional: buildings of a race or era, fortifications, temples, etc.
Complementary Skills: Region Lore or Historic Lore for styles, trends or typical layouts of a period; an appropriate Crafting skill when designing.
armor-maneuver:
Reduces the maneuver penalty for armor worn (Table 2.1l), but not any encumbrance penalty from the armor's weight, nor modifiers to ranged attacks or perception maneuvers. Normally used only to offset penalties.
Armor takes one round per -5 maneuver penalty to put on, and half that to remove (treat half a round as a 2 AP action). It can be put on in half the time, but then incurs an additional -20 armor maneuver penalty until the wearer takes the remaining time to adjust it properly.
Time Required: none for maneuvering in armor.
Specializations: none required. Optional: particular maneuvers (e.g., climbing, flanking on foot, swimming).
astronomy:
Identification of celestial objects and prediction of their movements; understanding of their nature varies by setting.
Utility is setting-dependent. If the stars truly reflect or influence events, it may predict events or assess personality (Astronomy = Astrology); then it may be complementary for social skills involving individuals whose birth circumstances are known.
May identify flows or tides of magical energy; at minimum complementary to Magical Ritual.
Time Required: 2-4 AP to identify celestial features or determine compass direction; 1 minute to determine latitude or time; at least 1 hour to predict celestial events.
Specializations: none required. Optional: astrology (and personality), divination, planetary motion, etc.
attunement:
Some items require attunement before using some or all abilities (unlike e.g. a +10 OB sword, whose bonus applies even unknowingly). Also a method of identifying items' magical powers. Forms a sympathetic bond between the auras of the individual and the item. Normally only one individual can be attuned to an item at a time; an individual may be attuned to any number of items.
Normally takes 3 minutes. Faster: 1 minute -10, half a minute -25, a single round -50. Attunement must occur before the round in which the item is used.
If Attunement fails, the item may not be attuned again until the character has improved their Attunement skill rank.
Attunement to allow use must be done by the user (not required for identification). One other character may aid by explaining the power(s) and via the Complementary Skill rule (adding their Attunement ranks); only one helper allowed.
Once attuned, spell abilities are used with a modified Spell-casting Roll (SCR) (Spell Law). More detail in Treasure Law.
Continuously-in-effect properties (including item bonuses) need no attunement. Intelligent items able to activate their own powers may not require it.
Time Required: 3 minutes at -0, 1 minute at -10, half a minute at -25, one round at -50. Using an already-attuned item, if an Attunement maneuver is required: 2-4 AP.
Specializations: none required. Possible: spell effects of a particular profession's base lists, spell effects of an element (e.g. light), etc.

Ranks plus realm stat (once) are added to the Spellcasting Roll.
The full skill bonus is used for Spell Mastery: changing the spell as it is cast (e.g. smaller Fire Ball, shaping a Wall of Fire). Other uses specified in certain spells. The difficulties below are for Spell Mastery. Casting modifiers: see Spell Law.

Time Required: spellcasting (including spell mastery) 2-4 AP, optionally concentration for each round of preparation. Instant spells: 0 AP (instantaneous actions).
Specializations: each Base, Open, Closed, Arcane or Restricted Spell List.
battle-styles:
Focus: Strength, armor and/or shield.
Specializations: Each specific Battle fighting style.
In all three, ranks may be allocated at the time of purchase to the abilities listed in the style.
blind-fighting:
A blinded combatant or one fighting in the dark has a penalty up to -100 (blindness or pitch black), offset by this skill. Lighting and visibility: Core Law section 15.7.
Can also offset darkness/visibility penalties for other active skills. Rule of thumb: a blind character (or in pitch dark) senses moving people and entities within 1' per rank, and terrain within half that distance. Moving more than that distance in a phase should be significantly harder. Fine detail or color may be impossible regardless of ranks.
Other senses may compensate: senses giving where a target is standing or moving (e.g. tremor sense) grant +20 to Blind Fighting; senses perceiving the target's outline (bat echolocation, life sense) grant +50.
Time Required: none. Unprepared characters moving from bright to dark may suffer greater visibility penalties for the first two minutes.
Specializations: none required. Optional: particular environments (forest, desert, indoors, etc.).
body-development:
Physical development: taking damage without being knocked out, extreme exertion or endurance.
Total hits = base hits (by race) + Body Development skill bonus. Small characters: total x0.75. Big: x1.5. Other sizes: Table 9-4a in Core Law section 9.4.
The Body Development bonus is used for Endurance rolls (Core Law section 5.5).
Death when negative hits exceed the Body Development bonus.
Time Required: none.
Specializations: none required. Optional: Endurance rolls in a particular activity (running, climbing, swimming). Specializations never affect hits.
channeling:
Transmits Power Points to a willing target or to an item made to store power. The sender must know the exact location of the target (seeing him, magical means, or prearranged appointment).
Sending: declare the PP sent, make a Medium (+0) Percentage Maneuver with Table 2.1d modifiers. Result = % of PP successfully transmitted (rest wasted). Result over 100 = bonus to the recipient's roll. Negative result: drains that many additional PP from the sender beyond the points sent (down to 0; further loss ignored).
Receiving: recipient makes a Medium (+0) Percentage Maneuver without the table modifiers. Result = % of transmitted PP actually gained (max 100% of PP sent). Recipient may exceed his normal maximum, but loses 1 PP per hour until at or below it.
Channeling a spell: much harder; both parties must succeed at an Absolute Maneuver. The spell is treated as cast by the recipient for range and area of effect, by the sender for all other purposes. Directed spells use the recipient's Directed Spells skill.
A charged item (e.g. wand) may be restored one charge by channeling that spell into it.
Items without skills of their own (non-sentient) always succeed on receiving power or spells, gaining 100% of the PP sent.
Time Required: 2-4 AP.
Specializations: none required. Optional: to or from a specific individual.
Complementary skills: Religion/Philosophy between the faithful; Power Projection when sending power short distances.
climbing:
From ladders to cliffs. Climbing speed = 1/4 of normal BMR, adjusted by pace as normal. Faster than Jog (x2) is not allowed unless there are plenty of obvious hand/footholds (ladder, tree) or the character has claws or is physically specialized for climbing.
If not at a stable point (e.g. a ledge to stand on), Concentration is required to hold position while taking any other action.
Difficulty depends mainly on grade (angle) and frequency of handholds. +1 difficulty level if sandy, +2 if wet, +3 if oily, +4 if icy.
Used for Dodging if attacked while climbing, but a Climbing roll is needed to keep a hold while dodging.
Fatigue checks normally every 6 rounds while climbing.
Rappelling (descending on a rope): rate equal to normal movement (with pace penalties if rushing). Failure may mean falling.
Time Required: a form of movement (see rate and pace above).
Specializations: none required. Optional: trees, walls, natural rocky surfaces, etc.

Ranks plus realm stat (once) are added to the Spellcasting Roll.

Specializations: each Base, Open, Closed, Arcane or Restricted Spell List.
combat-styles:
Focus: Speed and coordination.
Specializations: Each specific Combat fighting style.
In all three, ranks may be allocated at the time of purchase to the abilities listed in the style.
concealment:
Hiding items or groups of items of any size (weapon, building, campsite), or people, using the environment, lighting and camouflage; includes hiding items on one's person. An individual trying to remain unseen (moving or stationary) uses Stalking instead. Generally opposed by Perception.
Time Required (rule of thumb): 1 round miniscule item; 2 rounds diminutive (1-4 lbs); 3 rounds tiny (5-16 lbs); 4 rounds small (17-64 lbs); 5 rounds medium (a person); 1 minute big (a horse); double per size step above big. Less with preparation, more if the object fits poorly into the environment.
Specializations: none required. Optional: a type of object (herbs), a terrain (forest).
Complementary Skills: an applicable Survival specialization in the wild; Architecture when looking for hiding places in a building.
contortions:
Manipulating one's body to move through small openings or escape bonds. Difficulty from the opening's size relative to the character, or the bonds' material and how well they are secured. Also used to slip free of grapples (Core Law, Grapples, section 9.8).
An attempt to slip a grapple or bonds can be made every round until escape or an Absolute Failure, which tightens the grapple/bonds so the character cannot escape without assistance (may still try to incapacitate the grappler or break free with a feat of strength).
Slipping bonds is a full 4 AP action; each AP less than 4 gives a cumulative -25, minimum 1 AP at -75.
Slipping bonds or a grapple unobtrusively: -50, and a Stalking or Duping conflicting maneuver vs the observer's Perception (difficulty and modifiers by how closely the observer watches, light level, etc.).
Absorbing an impact (e.g. a collision): reduces the critical by one severity; requires 1-4 AP.
Time Required: 1-4 AP.
Specializations: none required. Optional: escape, tunnel-crawling, etc.
Complementary Skills: Wrestling when escaping a grapple.
control-lycanthropy:
Lycanthropic shape changing is provoked by instinct and emotion, controlled through discipline and calm; the urge follows the lunar cycle, hardest to resist at the full moon.
An Absolute Maneuver with this skill (-25 if 0 ranks) is rolled each time the character goes to sleep on a full moon, whenever the character displays real rage, and whenever the GM judges extreme emotional stress. Failure: transforms into bestial form; the lycanthrope (GM-controlled) hunts, kills and feeds, violently attacking anyone interfering; once sated it hides and sleeps, reverts to "human" form and awakens in control, with no memory of the transformation or its actions.
Deliberate change into bestial form keeping control: additional -25. Controlled beast back to "human" form: additional -50. Failure at either: slips into the uncontrolled state above.
Physical stress and trauma (injury and fatigue penalties) apply as penalties; GM assesses mental/emotional stresses too. Meditation, sedative herbs/drugs or magic giving bonuses to calm or self-discipline give bonuses.
Time Required: 0-2 AP to resist transforming; 2-4 AP to transform deliberately.
Specializations: none required.
Complementary Skills: Survival or an applicable Animal Handling skill when attempting to take animal form; Religion/Philosophy when attempting to avoid it.
creature-lore:
Recognition, habitat, diet, powers and abilities of a specific type of creature; higher ranks cover cultures, psychology and other details; scholars may recognize indirect signs of the creatures' influence.
Natural creatures and plants (including magical variants such as giant insects, mistravens, flying monkeys, griffons): use Survival for the biome. Creatures forming societies and cultures: Racial Lore. Some creatures fall under several skills (e.g. champions: Creature Lore (Extra-Planar Creatures) and Religion/Philosophy Lore).
Time Required: remembering facts from own knowledge is a free action. Identifying a creature may also need a Perception maneuver if not clearly visible (distance, dark). Book research may take an hour or more.
Specializations (setting-dependent, typically):
• Artificial Creatures: constructs, golems, magically animated gargoyles and other magically created creatures.
• Demons: Demons, Agothu, Chaos Demons.
• Dragons: all Fell Creatures, including dragons, basilisks, dragonkin, drakes, wyrms.
• Elementals: creatures of pure elemental matter and elemental creatures (ice spiders, phoenixes, zephyr hounds).
• Extra-Planar Creatures: otherworldly creatures not in another category (champions, genies, Visitors).
• Faerie: all fey creatures (gremlins, sylphs, ellyllon, pooka, etc.).
• Undead: creatures persisting after bodily death.
Complementary skills: Survival for the creature's biome, or Region Lore for a region where the creature is common or well known.
culinary:
Preparing food and beverages. Success normally gives a pleasant product. Failure is unpleasant or may waste the ingredients; normally only an Absolute Failure can be harmful.
Time Required: preparing a meal 30 minutes to 2 hours depending on complexity.
Specializations: not normally required. Optional: cook, brewer, sommelier, butcher, cheese maker, etc.
Complementary Skills: Region Lore for dishes of a particular culture.
directed-spell:
Provides the OB for magical attacks directed or aimed at a target; does not create the attack (requires casting an applicable spell).
To develop a Directed Spell specialization, the character must be able to cast a suitable spell at least once per day (intrinsically, from an item, or from runes).
Normal ranged attack modifiers apply.
No benefit for ball or cone spells (Core Law section 9.3 Area Attacks).
Time Required: part of the spellcasting maneuver (2-4 AP); no additional AP.
Specializations:
• Elemental Bolts: bolts of elemental energy (e.g. Shock Bolt, Lightning Bolt).
• Illusionary Attacks: attacks by illusions with a physical aspect (e.g. Phantasms including a feel sense, Strike I).
• Hurling: throwing physical objects with telekinesis or similar (e.g. Hurling).
disarm:
Forces an opponent to drop his weapon, or takes it. Resolved as a conflicting maneuver: the disarmer rolls as a normal attack (including any penalty from the target parrying the attacker) with the additional penalties of Table 2.1f, offset by this skill. The defender makes a defense roll (no action required) as if an attack roll (subtracting any parry used); any amount over 100 is an additional penalty to the attacker's disarm roll. Details: disarming, Core Law section 9.7.
Natural attacks cannot be disarmed, but this skill may offset the called shot penalty (normally -25) for a melee attack against an appendage or body part making a natural attack (e.g. the head of a biting creature). The Disarm bonus is halved for this (+40 needed to fully offset the -20 called shot penalty), and none of the normal Disarm penalties apply.
Time Required: 2-4 AP.
Specializations: none required. Optional: disarming a specific type of weapon (dagger, short sword, etc.).
discipline-styles:
Focus: Adrenal maneuvers or unarmed martial arts.
Specializations: Each specific Discipline fighting style.
In all three, ranks may be allocated at the time of purchase to the abilities listed in the style.
drawing-painting:
Visual art from realistic to abstract. Fine work may need a pencil, pen, brush or similar; crude work possible with any surface, some pigment and a finger.
Also other visual expression: calligraphy, make-up, forgery, etc. Forgeries are normally conflicting: forger's Drawing/Painting vs the observer's relevant Lore or Vocation.
Time Required: a quick sketch about a minute; a great masterpiece months or years.
Specializations: none required. Optional: an artistic style (oil painting), subject matter (portraits), mapmaking, calligraphy, official-looking documents (forgery), make-up (cosmetics, disguise), drafting (blueprints).
Complementary Skills: Lore skills for the subject matter; Administration vocations for official-looking documents; Navigation for mapmaking; Medicine for simulating injuries with cosmetics.
engineering:
Mathematics, physics and invention: theoretical knowledge of devices and processes and why they work. Used to determine what a device does, design new devices or streamline systems.
In more advanced cultures the GM may require specialization; not needed in fantasy settings (basic mechanical and hydraulic engineering).
State of the art is setting-dependent; even a historical medieval setting allows complicated mechanical devices (clockwork, water mills, windmills, sawmills).
Time Required: see the examples for assessments; designing new devices takes days to months depending on complexity.
Specializations: none required.
Complementary Skills: Mathematics, or the skills needed to use the products (e.g. Piloting when designing or studying a vehicle).
fabric-craft:
Spinning cloth from animal or vegetable fibers and making it into clothes.
Crafting superior armor (including costs): see Treasure Law.
Time Required: highly variable, minutes to days; when creating items, see the production times on the equipment lists. Assessing item quality generally takes one minute.
Specializations: not normally required; could include spinster, dyer, tailor, weaver, seamstress, tapestry knotter, hatter, rope braider, etc.
flying:
Flight speed depends on a base movement rate (usually defined by the means of flight) and a selected pace. While flying, Sprint pace is "Diving" (only achievable by rapidly descending) and Dash is "Power Diving" (flying as hard as possible while rapidly descending).
Flying creatures can glide at up to Run pace at half the normal movement penalties. Unless conditions are ideal (strong thermals or updrafts), every round of continued gliding requires a successful maneuver at a cumulative -10 per round.
Depending on the method of flight, Concentration may be required to maintain flight while taking other actions. Not required for naturally flying species or magical flight with the Fly spell or equivalents; may be required for unnatural winged flight (e.g., the Wings spell).
Used for Dodging if the character is attacked while in flight.
Charging attacks in flight require the Swooping talent (see Creature Law).
Time Required: a movement skill; speed and whether Concentration is required depend on the method of flight. Magical flight normally does not require movement (hovering is possible), but speed varies with the spell.
Specializations: the specific method of flying (e.g., wings, hang glider, magical flight).
footwork:
Movement during other actions incurs a pace penalty: -25 for Walk (x1), -50 for Jog (x2), -75 for Run (x3). Footwork offsets this penalty for movement during melee or thrown weapon attacks.
Time Required: used as part of an attack action; no additional AP.
Specializations: none required. A specific weapon is too broad to be a suitable specialization unless restricted to a particular circumstance, such as charging or chasing.
fortitude:
Temporarily blocks pain and discomfort. With a successful maneuver, all penalties due to fatigue, hit loss, injuries and Stun are halved. The character is still considered Stunned for attacks against them and for concentration.
Instantaneous action. Benefits apply in the same round and continue one additional round for every full 20 the maneuver succeeded by (total of 1 round on 101-120, 2 rounds on 121-140).
All injury penalties apply to every Fortitude maneuver, even after successful use of Fortitude.
Resolved on the Adrenal maneuvers table:
• Absolute Failure: additional Fatigue penalty of -20.
• Partial Success: penalties reduced by one quarter (e.g., -80 becomes -60).
• Absolute Success: no fatigue, hit loss, injury or stun penalties during the first round (all penalties removed for the first round).
Time Required: 0 AP (instantaneous action) for the first round; none for additional rounds if the maneuver succeeded by at least 20.
Specializations: none required.
Complementary Skills: Medicine, by the character or an ally, to minimize the pain.
grace:
Reduces penalties for casting spells above the caster's level (overcasting). The penalty is normally -20 per level of the spell above the caster's level.
Time Required: part of a spellcasting action (2-4 AP), no additional AP. Overcasting always requires a minimum of one round of spell preparation (except instantaneous spells).
Specializations: each specific spell list.
herbalism:
Knowledge of effects and doses, preparation and application of herbs and medicines. Searching for herbs uses Survival for the appropriate biome (Herbalism may be Complementary). Detailed herb rules: Treasure Law. In higher tech societies may be replaced with Pharmacology.
Time Required: preparing an herb depends on its preparation type: Apply 1-10 rounds, Brew 20 minutes, Liquid 1-10 rounds, Paste 10 minutes, Powder 5 minutes. 2-4 AP to identify an herb or remember facts from your own knowledge; book research may take an hour or more.
Specializations: none required. Optional: herbs of a specific biome, or to treat a specific type of injury (e.g., herbs that treat bleeding).
Complementary Skills: Medicine, when the purpose is to treat an injury.
historic-lore:
Knowledge of recorded events of history. The broader the geography and era purchased, the less specific the information; the narrower, the more specific but only for that area/era (e.g., "History of the Northern Continent" applies widely but gives broad information; "History of the Shulin Kai during the Third Imperial Era" is detailed but limited).
History contains partial truths or falsehoods: recalling a detail known to few, while the majority believes a commonly held "story", may require an Absolute Success.
Time Required: free action to remember facts from your own knowledge; book research may take an hour or more.
Specializations: a specific region and/or time period.
Complementary Skills: an appropriate Region Lore or Racial Lore will often apply.
illusion-crafting:
Crafting illusions to ensure verisimilitude or imitate real creatures, items or individuals (deception), or to entertain or support other performances (e.g., acoustic resonance or lighting for a speech, covering shabby props on a stage).
Time Required: part of the spellcasting maneuver (2-4 AP), no additional AP.
Specializations: none required. Optional: specific subject matter (e.g., illusions of humans). Spell Artistry may be developed as an alternative specialization, applying to elaborate and artful uses of Spell Mastery rather than illusions (Spell Law section 4.6).
Complementary Skills: an appropriate Lore skill when creating an illusion of an object, structure or creature covered by that Lore; Acting for illusions of people; Animal Handling or Survival for illusions of animals or creatures.
influence:
Bonus to maneuvers that shift people's opinions in the direction the character desires (Core Law chapter 14).
Speech to a larger audience: as a rule of thumb, direct effects on 10% of the audience and indirect effects on the entire audience.
Time Required: minimum 2-4 AP; difficulty is typically lower if more time is spent.
Specializations: Charm, Duping, or Intimidation.
• Charm: approaching and interacting with people so they like you and do you "favors". More groundwork makes it work better. Getting something for nothing; once it becomes "I'll do you a favor if you do me a favor", use Trading instead. Useful for working crowds for information or carousing.
• Duping: lying, bluffing, dissembling or spinning the truth convincingly. Acting or a suitable Vocation skill may be Complementary. Can distract a foe in (potential) combat, persuade someone that an action is reasonable when it is not, or get a target to talk by making them think it is safe or advantageous.
• Intimidation: getting what you want by subtle or overt threat without making the target flee for help or fight back (and without provoking a fear or morale reaction). May also be used to deliberately provoke a fear or morale reaction: the number of ranks is the attack level for the recipient's fear RR (Core Law sections 14.2 and 14.3). The threat need not be physical (blackmail, violence, vandalism, legal action, curses or magic, social influence) but must be credible: an easily believed threat reduces the difficulty, one that does not seem credible may significantly increase it.
jumping:
Covers running and standing jumps. Every character has a base jump distance per jump type (Table 2.1h). "Stride" is the character's stride modifier read in inches (e.g., halflings use a stride modifier of -5").
Difficulty modifier to jump a specific distance: +40, minus 20 for each full multiple of the applicable base jump:
• Modifier = +40 (- 20 * (Distance / base jump))
If the maneuver fails but the actual distance jumped matters, use the Percentage Maneuver table (Core Law Table 5-1) to determine the distance.
A running high jump may be used to clear an obstacle (e.g., a hurdle) without stopping.
Pole vault (flexible but strong pole): requires a sprint (no standing pole vaults). Running long base jump x2; running high base jump x5.
Time Required: part of movement, no additional AP beyond the distance traveled.
Specializations: none required.
language-sign:
Determines the ability to communicate in or understand a language. Must be specialized as written, spoken or signaled versions of a language. Non-spoken communication (codes, sign language, flag signals, etc.) counts as a language.
Normally fluency is determined by the number of ranks: most languages are proficient at 4-6 ranks; some simple languages or codes need only a few ranks (e.g., Morse code). Ranks beyond 10 cover variations over time or by region; scholars could recognize or recite important speeches or famous written works. Details: Core Law section 3.13.
Even with basic fluency, stress or rushing may cause confusion (tense diplomacy, fast talking, strong accents, dialects): treat as a Percentage Maneuver with a situational difficulty; the GM garbles the words to reflect the percentage of success. Each new phrase is treated the same way; if someone keeps repeating the same exact words, further PM rolls add up as normal.
Time Required: variable.
Specializations: each written, spoken or signed language; also hand signs, signals (e.g., flags or semaphore) or codes (e.g., Morse code). For all signals, and for codes and non-verbal communication intended to be discreet, halve the effective number of ranks.

leadership:
Inspires those loyal to you to follow instructions, or effectively organizes a group. Cannot be used on those not already loyal to you.
Any instruction or command that might be resisted or questioned (i.e., requires a morale check, Core Law section 14.3) is modified by your Leadership bonus.
All combatants who consider you their leader get a bonus equal to your Leadership ranks to RRs vs. Fear/Terror, as long as they are aware you are present.
The leader may make a maneuver to rally followers affected by a failed fear check (Core Law section 14.3); modifiers in Table 2.1i.
Also applies when working with others to accomplish a task more quickly (Complementary Skills, Core Law chapter 3).
Time Required: the Fear RR bonus (equal to ranks) applies simply by being present. A rally maneuver is a 2-4 AP action.
Specializations: none required.
Complementary Skills: Leadership may be Complementary for any effort to coordinate multiple individuals in a task (e.g., collectively searching an area), and for tactical battlefield maneuvers (e.g., using Running to get into a foe's flank).
leathercraft:
Curing animal hide and making leather items.
Crafting superior armor (including costs): see Treasure Law.
Time Required: highly variable, minutes to days; see production times on the equipment lists. Assessing item quality generally takes one minute.
Specializations: not normally required; could include tanner, leather worker, saddler, cobbler, tent maker, armorer, girdler, etc.
locks:
Manipulating and picking locks without a key, maintaining locks, changing user-adjustable locks, designing locks (manufacturing one requires an appropriate Crafting skill).
Special tools or circumstances (special materials; broken, jammed or seized lock; anything beyond normal) may increase or decrease the difficulty.
Time Required: Easy and Light locks 2 rounds, Medium 4, Hard 8, Very Hard 1 minute, Extremely Hard 2 minutes. Absolute Success takes half the time; each Partial Success requires another time increment.
Specializations: none required.
magic-ritual:
Alternative way to use magic: compared to spells, rituals may be broad in effect but usually take much longer. The listed specializations are representative, not comprehensive.
Some spell effects fall into two types (e.g., Shield is defensive but works by creating a temporary barrier object, so either a Creation or Defensive ritual could produce it). See Spell Law chapter 5.
Time Required: see Spell Law.
Specializations: Alteration, Creation, Defensive, Destruction, Elemental, Healing, Informational, or Summoning & Transportation.
materials-lore:
Knowledge of a specific type of material: identification of the raw material, sources and methods of working (crafting itself uses a Crafting skill). May include famous magical, historic, legendary or cursed materials and items made from them.
Time Required: free action to remember facts from your own knowledge; book research may take an hour or more; at least one minute to appraise an item.
Specializations: Bone/horn, Fabrics, Leather, Metal, Stone, or Wood.
Complementary Skills: Historic Lore when assessing items of historic note; applicable crafting skills.
mathematics:
From counting and basic arithmetic up to more abstract manipulations; many other sciences depend on adequate mathematical skill.
In many medieval societies common folk may lack basic mathematics: characters with no ranks may have trouble beyond counting on fingers (and toes). Scholars and engineers may know algebra, geometry and proto-calculus techniques, possibly entwined with basic physics (e.g., trajectories).
Time Required: variable; rule of thumb one minute for a Medium calculation, doubling for each additional difficulty level.
Specializations: none required. Optional: geometry, accounting, probability, physics, etc.
Complementary Skills: Administration for bookkeeping; Engineering for some analytical purposes.
mechanics:
Operation, repair and construction of technology. In most fantasy settings a single skill covering all mechanical and hydraulic (pump) devices; at higher tech levels it should become increasingly specialized.
Operation: proper use of technological constructs, getting maximum results and avoiding overstressing them to breakage. Can operate parts of a vehicle not in motion; in motion the vehicle requires Piloting.
Repair & Construction: assembling constructs from parts, identifying jams, replacing damaged parts. Constructing or repairing broken parts requires an appropriate crafting skill; crafting new, original devices requires Engineering (Science).
Time Required: operating a device requires 2-4 AP to begin and may require Concentration to continue. Moderate repairs: about 10% of the device's production time; 5% or less if production required fabricating precision parts and spares are available.
Specializations: Operation, Repair & Construction.
Complementary Skills: Engineering.
medicine:
Bonus for treating injuries and overt symptoms of illness, including simple medical aids/herbs, setting broken bones, stopping bleeding. Quick reference in Table 2.1m; full injury and healing rules in Core Law section 13.1.
Specializations: none required. Optional: treatment of poisons, diseases, bone-setting, etc.
meditation:
Enter and exploit a mental trance to help solve difficult problems or perform mental maneuvers. The character must meditate for 5 minutes; with a successful maneuver they get +25 the following round to all mental actions (attuning to a magic item, casting a spell, using a lore skill, etc.).
Time Required: 5 minutes. Increase the difficulty by three levels to complete the meditation in 1 minute.
Specializations: none required. Optional: a specific type of mental maneuver (e.g., lore, casting spells, attunement).
melee-weapon:
Wielding any melee weapon in combat (see Core Law). May also be used to assess the quality of a weapon (difficulties below).
Time Required: melee attacks are a 2-4 AP action. Evaluating a weapon takes one minute.
Specializations: Blade, Chain, Hafted, Greater Blade, Greater Chain, Greater Hafted, Pole Arm, or any specific Exotic weapon type (e.g., whip).
mental-focus:
Maintaining concentration for extended periods (Core Law section 5.5), while stunned, or when concentrating on two things at once (Core Law section 8.1). The GM may also require a Mental Focus roll in extremely stressful, chaotic or confusing situations.
Time Required: normally used to maintain concentration; no additional time.
Specializations: none required.
metalcraft:
Unearthing ore, melting and refining it into ingots or billets, and molding or working metal objects (iron, copper, silver, gold, etc.).
Crafting metal items normally requires tools; without tools, increase the difficulty by at least 3 difficulty levels.
Crafting superior items (including costs): see Treasure Law.
Time Required: highly variable, minutes to days; see production times on the equipment lists. Assessing item quality generally takes one minute.
Specializations: none required. Optional: blacksmith, copper smith, foundry worker, jeweler, gold smith, silver smith, weapon smith, armorer, etc.
mounted-combat:
Actions by a mounted combatant incur a penalty up to -125 based on the mount's pace (Table 2.1p). This skill offsets those penalties when making attacks. It does not cover controlling the mount (Riding). See Mounted Combat, Core Law section 9.7.
Charging on horseback increases the effective size of the attack (Table 2.1p).
Time Required: none.
Specializations: none required. Optional: use of a specific weapon. "Horse" is too broad to be an acceptable specialization.
multiple-attacks:
Makes multiple attacks as a single attack action. With multiple weapons, up to one attack per weapon; an unarmed attack is also possible with any limb not wielding a weapon (e.g., a kick). Multiple attacks with the same weapon or limb in a single attack action are not possible. See Katas, Core Law section 9.7.
Any penalty not cancelled by Multiple Attacks applies equally to every attack. Sufficient skill can completely cancel the penalties but never grants a bonus.
Time Required: a melee attack action is 2-4 AP; multiple attacks do not change it.
Specializations: none required.
music:
Performing music (sheet music or improvisation) on a specific instrument, or singing.
Used to entertain or earn a living, or to evoke a mood or even actions (e.g., stirring up hostility against a noble). Complementary when used to make a subject more responsive to influence; if the music itself delivers the persuasive message (e.g., songs of rebellion), it may replace Influence or Leadership.
Time Required: duration of the music performed.
Specializations: Singing, each group of instruments (drums, flutes, woodwinds, horns), dance (use Agility in place of Memory as the stat).
Complementary Skills: Region Lore or Racial Lore when pleasing an audience of a particular region or race; Influence or Leadership when using Music to persuade.
music-composition:
Creating new works and adapting old ones (Music performs known pieces). Music influences a single audience; a composition may influence many audiences if it catches on and is disseminated. A well-crafted composition may reduce the difficulty of a subsequent related Music maneuver.
Also used to recognize a piece of music, its style, or its composer.
Time Required: variable, from minutes for a simple melody to weeks or months for elaborate symphonies or operas for very large ensembles.
Specializations: none required. Optional: each style of music (classical, baroque, romantic, jazz, etc.).
Complementary Skills: Music; Writing when composing a piece with lyrics.
navigation:
Determining proper directions and distances when using or creating a map with a directional aid (compass, stars). Includes orienteering; applies on land or water. Getting around by familiar landmarks uses Region Lore instead.
Time Required: normally conducted as part of long-distance travel. Determining location at a given moment during ongoing navigation: one round. If unprepared and needing the location immediately: 5 rounds.
Specializations: none required. Possible: on land, at sea, underground, etc.
Complementary Skills: Region Lore (knowing a few landmarks helps); Astronomy when stars are visible.
open-spell-list:
Ranks in a list = the level up to which the character can cast from it (e.g. 8 ranks in Fire Law: any spell up to 8th level, though spells above his own level may be difficult).
Ranks plus realm stat (once) are added to the Spellcasting Roll.
The full skill bonus is used for Spell Mastery: changing the spell as it is cast (e.g. smaller Fire Ball, shaping a Wall of Fire). Other uses specified in certain spells. The difficulties below are for Spell Mastery. Casting modifiers: see Spell Law.
Five Spell List skills, each list a specialization:
• Base: the specialized lists of each magic-using profession.
• Open: common, straightforward spells understood by anyone of the realm.
• Closed: more esoteric techniques, understood by any user of the realm but with greater difficulty.
• Arcane: obscure or exotic magics outside the three realms.
• Restricted: any list the GM allows that is not Base, Open, Closed or Arcane (e.g. another profession's Base list).
Lists from realms other than your own cannot be developed.
Time Required: spellcasting (including spell mastery) 2-4 AP, optionally concentration for each round of preparation. Instant spells: 0 AP (instantaneous actions).
Specializations: each Base, Open, Closed, Arcane or Restricted Spell List.
perception:
Noticing details about the environment and interpreting them: finding hidden objects, noticing imperfections that may hide a secret door, noticing trap triggers, sensing potential ambushes. Includes all senses; if a particular sense is required there may be a modifier for a superior (or inferior) sense.
If a character states he is watching or examining an area, situation or place, the GM makes an Absolute Maneuver roll with the character's Perception (may be secret, revealing only what was observed). A heavy penalty (if a roll is allowed at all) applies when the players do not know what they are looking for or do not specify looking for something in particular (looking for ceiling traps makes it difficult to see pit traps, etc.).
Often used as a conflicting skill against Stalking or Concealment.
Time Required: 0-2 AP for a normal Perception check; longer for an extensive search.
Specializations: none required. Optional: specific focused situations, e.g., scouting awareness (on point for the party), guard awareness (standing watch), sleep awareness (waking quickly after a disturbance), ambush awareness, a specific environment such as a biome (e.g., temperate forest) or urban areas (muggers, pickpockets, oncoming vehicles), a specific sense (hearing, smell), or a magical means of detection (e.g., scrying).
piloting:
Operating a vehicle (wagon, cart, sleigh, blimp, etc.): controls, braking, performance across terrain. For animal-drawn vehicles the driver should also have Animal Handling to control the animal.
The maneuver may be modified by vehicle speed, angle of turn, and approximate size and maneuverability (Table 2.1r).
Animal-powered vehicles are generally not very maneuverable and the GM-assigned difficulty should reflect it; right angle turns are not possible (the rear of the cart continues straight until pulled into the curve). Sail-powered ships are limited in turning angle and cannot sail directly against the wind; rowed boats can rotate in place.
Time Required: 2-4 AP per round during maneuvers. No activity normally required when continuing at constant speed and direction, except human-powered vehicles (e.g., rowboats), which normally require Concentration while in motion.
Specializations: each specific type of vehicle.
Complementary Skills: Animal Handling for a maneuver that is primarily Piloting an animal-drawn vehicle; an appropriate Survival specialization for any type of ship or boat.
poison-mastery:
Knowledge of effects and doses, preparation and application of health-destroying chemicals or diseases, and preparation and application of antidotes. See Treasure Law section 2.3.
Time Required: 2-4 AP to remember facts from your own knowledge; book research may take an hour or more. Preparing a poison depends on its form: powders 5 minutes, liquids 1-10 rounds, pastes 10 minutes.
Specializations: none required. Optional: poisons native to a specific biome, or a category of poison (e.g., respiratory, paralytic).
Complementary Skills: Survival for the biome where a poison is found; Medicine when aiding someone who has been poisoned; Culinary when hiding a poison in food or drink.
power-development:
The total skill bonus determines the number of Power Points available for spell casting. Each character has a single PP pool, even with access to multiple realms.
PP are recovered through rest: 10% of the PP total per 2 hours of sleep, up to a full night of sleep (8 hours per day). Characters needing more or less sleep recover proportionally faster or slower, but only up to the limit of a full night (e.g., a character needing 4 hours recovers 10% per hour, up to 4 hours). Recovery rate may vary with the campaign Power Level (Core Law section 12.1). A fully expended caster needs more than one night to recover.
Time Required: none.
Specializations: none required or possible.
power-projection:
Projects magical power and counters opponents' projections, creating a visible construct of magical energy between the opponents (a ball of power, a strand of light) held until one participant fails.
Duel procedure:
• Opponents must be within 30' of each other; they enter combat rounds and roll initiative each round.
• Each participant, on their initiative, expends 1 PP each round and makes a Routine Absolute Maneuver with this skill.
• Neither participant may perform any action other than conversation and casual perception while engaged.
• From the second round, the maneuver takes a cumulative -20 each round it is held active.
• A participant who cannot (out of PP) or will not contribute more PP, moves beyond 30', or is stunned, is treated as a failure result.
• Once a participant loses control (by any of the above or by failing a check) and the failure penalties are resolved, the contest ends; the other participant wins and is untouched and unharmed by the loser's failure, with no further rolls.
Normally modified only for the number of rounds; advanced techniques are listed in the example difficulties.
Time Required: 4 AP per round. May be reduced to Concentration with a -50 penalty (see Sheer Folly below).
Specializations: none required.
Alternate usage: detecting active power (active spells) and "catching" incoming spells (see below).
protect:
A combatant may parry or use a shield to protect an ally, sacrificing offense to interpose. The protector must be within melee range of both combatants and takes an OB penalty by position (Table 2.1s), offset by Protect skill.
The protector may designate any part of his parry or shield DB as protecting the defended combatant instead of himself, and may wait until the attack is declared before deciding.
Protecting multiple allies: sum of the penalties for each ally (e.g. two allies both beside the protector: -50 each, -100 total).
Time Required: part of an attack action (2-4 AP); no additional time.
Specializations: none required.
racial-lore:
Recognition, habitat, diet, powers and abilities of a specific race; higher ranks cover cultures, psychology and other details. Overlaps substantially with Region Lore where a region is mainly inhabited by one race.
Can distinguish the different cultures of a race, or tell which traits are culturally specific vs shared by most of the race.
Time Required: free action to remember facts from own knowledge. Identifying a creature not clearly visible (distance, dark...) may also need a Perception maneuver. Book research: an hour or more.
Specializations: Elf, Halfling, Human, Orc, etc.
Complementary Skills: Region Lore, Historic Lore or Creature Lore, in various situations.
ranged-weapon:
Wielding muscle-powered thrown weapons and mechanical devices firing low-velocity projectiles. For combat use see Core Law; the difficulties below are for evaluating a weapon's quality.
Time Required: 1-3 AP to make a ranged attack. One minute to assess a weapon's quality.
Specializations: Bow, Crossbow, Sling, Thrown, or a specific Exotic weapon.
region-lore:
Geography of a region plus a basic overview of local cultures, flora, fauna and limited history. Region no more than 100,000 square miles (about 300 x 300 miles).
Also used when navigating by local landmarks or familiarity with the area.
Time Required: free action to remember facts from own knowledge. Finding your way may also need a Perception maneuver if landmarks are not clearly visible. Book research: an hour or more.
Specializations: each specific region.
Complementary Skills: Historic Lore, or Racial Lore for races of the area.
religion-lore:
Taken generally (basics of all religions/philosophies the character is familiar with) or about a single religion (more specifics). Mostly theory, dogma and belief, plus structure of organized religions or philosophical societies; touches on history.
Time Required: free action to remember facts from own knowledge. Book research: an hour or more.
Specializations: a specific religion or philosophy, or a specific region covering all religions practiced there.
Complementary Skills: Historic Lore or Region Lore for a religion of that region.
restricted-quarters:
Combat in restricted spaces incurs a penalty from -25 to -100 (Table 2.1t), offset by this skill. See Restricted Quarters in Core Law section 9.5.
Restrictions come from small spaces, many obstructions (e.g. ship rigging), being surrounded by a crowd, or being pressed by foes on all sides (especially foes with shields or shorter weapons).
• Close: room to stand but limited room to maneuver or swing a weapon.
• Cramped: forced to crouch or squeeze through spaces too narrow to stand normally.
• Tight: must crawl; weapon movement severely restricted.
• Confined: belly-crawling through an extremely narrow space.
Restrictions may be less severe with a suitable very small weapon (e.g. dagger) and more severe with a large or unsuitable one (e.g. pole arm, flail).
Time Required: aids an attack action (2-4 AP); no additional time.
Specializations: none required; optional: any Combat Training specialization.
restricted-spell-list:
Ranks in a list = the level up to which the character can cast from it (e.g. 8 ranks in Fire Law: any spell up to 8th level, though spells above his own level may be difficult).
Ranks plus realm stat (once) are added to the Spellcasting Roll.
The full skill bonus is used for Spell Mastery: changing the spell as it is cast (e.g. smaller Fire Ball, shaping a Wall of Fire). Other uses specified in certain spells. The difficulties below are for Spell Mastery. Casting modifiers: see Spell Law.
Five Spell List skills, each list a specialization:
• Base: the specialized lists of each magic-using profession.
• Open: common, straightforward spells understood by anyone of the realm.
• Closed: more esoteric techniques, understood by any user of the realm but with greater difficulty.
• Arcane: obscure or exotic magics outside the three realms.
• Restricted: any list the GM allows that is not Base, Open, Closed or Arcane (e.g. another profession's Base list).
Lists from realms other than your own cannot be developed.
Time Required: spellcasting (including spell mastery) 2-4 AP, optionally concentration for each round of preparation. Instant spells: 0 AP (instantaneous actions).
Specializations: each Base, Open, Closed, Arcane or Restricted Spell List.
reverse-strike:
Attacks against foes on one's own flank suffer -30, to the rear -70; offset by this skill.
Alternatively, reduces the positional bonus a foe gets for attacking from the flank (+15) or rear (+35); used this way, Reverse Strike is halved. Against multiple foes, divide the Reverse Strike skill by the number of foes warded against. See Core Law section 9.5.
Time Required: aids an attack action (2-4 AP); no additional time.
Specializations: none required; optional: any Combat Training specialization.
riding:
Staying on the mount safely and controlling it.
Unskilled rider (no ranks): can perform no actions other than perception and conversation while the mount moves; no control (the animal must be led or goes where it pleases). Horses in a moving mounted group follow the "herd" until spooked or threatened, then flee (with the group if all flee, otherwise away from what scared it).
If the mount moves faster than a walk, an unskilled rider must at least partially succeed on a riding maneuver (usual -25 for 0 ranks) every round to avoid being thrown.
Complex riding maneuvers or controlling the mount in stressful situations: riding maneuver with a modifier of half the pace penalty. Other actions while mounted suffer the full pace penalty of the mount's movement (see Mounted Combat).
Used instead of Leadership for Fear Resistance Rolls and rallying frightened mounts (Core Law section 14.3).
Time Required: a simple order to a well-trained animal is a free action, or 4 AP if untrained in riding. Persuading a mount to act against its nature (jumping, moving towards immediate danger such as combat): 0-2 AP.
Specializations: each type of animal or creature that can be ridden.
Alternate Usage: a mounted character may use Riding instead of other movement skills (e.g. Running) for Dodging. No roll needed.
runes:
With the Rune Mastery or Sacred Runes spell list, spells are stored as "runes" (on enchanted Rune Paper or an equivalent) for later use by anyone with this skill.
Casting a spell from a rune requires a successful Runes maneuver to decipher it first. If the Runes maneuver fails, the item cannot be used until the character has improved his Runes skill rank.
Level of effect = level of the spell inscribed; can be raised by using a higher-level Rune spell than needed (e.g. Sleep V inscribed with Rune VI is resisted as 6th level). For an elemental attack, the reader's appropriate Directed Spell OB is used.
Casting from a rune is like normal casting, except the caster may add ranks in Runes as well as any ranks in the list the spell comes from. Other details in Spell Law.
Time Required: using the rune takes the normal casting time (2-4 AP). Deciphering in advance: 3 minutes, no penalty; 1 minute: -10; a single round: -25; simultaneously with casting: -50 to the Runes roll and -20 to the casting (and the stored spell may not be what was expected).
Specializations: none required; optional: runes storing spells of a particular profession, element, etc.
running:
Main movement skill for ground-based races: moving at any pace (Creep through Dash) on foot; also used for evasive dodging on foot (Core Law section 9.6), though Acrobatics may be used instead.
Running maneuvers are not normally required except in difficult circumstances or to resolve a conflict (e.g. outmaneuvering another).
Fatigue checks while moving: every 2 hours at Walk, every 5 minutes at Jog, every minute at Run, every two rounds at Sprint, every round at Dash.
Time Required: part of movement; no additional time.
Specializations: default Running. Alternatives: other ground movement (skiing, skating, stilts). Evasive dodging is too broad to be a specialization.
service:
Vocations focused on interaction and providing services: presenting and conducting oneself in business and finding clients.
Many service vocations need other skills (Innkeeper: Trading or Culinary; Guide: Region Lore; Researcher: Lore or Science), often usable as Complementary skills; e.g. Service: Bodyguard is complementary to Perception while protecting a client.
Pleasing a customer: difficulty depends on their demeanor, mood and requirements. If the service only needs to be provided without pleasing the customer, difficulty may be several levels easier.
Vocation skills are a catch-all for minor occupational skills; they do not replace several other skills with one. Also useful when impersonating or persuading a member of the occupation.
Time Required: highly variable.
Specializations: Advocate/Barrister, Bodyguard, Bonesetter, Casino Dealer/Croupier, Guardsman, Guide, Innkeeper, Researcher, Shaman, Sailor, Soldier, Teacher, Valet, etc.
shield:
More defensive benefit from a shield in melee or against ranged attacks (Core Law section 9.6). Covers defending and shield bash attacks, but not both in the same round. Shield bash simultaneously with a weapon attack: see Katas, Core Law section 9.7 (penalties mitigated by Multiple Attacks skill).
Base shield DB applies against area attacks if the shield is oriented towards the attack; blocking DB (passive, partial or full) does not.
For combat use see Core Law; difficulties below are for evaluating a shield's quality with this skill alone.
Time Required: passive blocking: no time or AP. Partial blocking: concentration. Full blocking: 4 AP.
Specializations: default Shield. Alternatively Main Gauche: defensive use of any offhand parrying or blocking weapon. Used solely to defend, such a weapon gives +5 DB plus the ranks in this skill, as a shield, but only against melee attacks (not ranged). If the weapon attacks, no defensive benefit that round. (See also Defensive Ward in Chapter 4 Fighting Styles.)
Restricting Blocking (optional rule, see Running): full blocking DB bonus = Shield rank bonus, half while partial blocking; full blocking is a full round action (rather than 4 AP).
social-awareness:
Awareness of motives and social maneuvers of others: study people, determine if they are lying, infer motives.
If someone is using this skill (not relaxed with guard down) when targeted by an Influence maneuver, he can make a conflicting maneuver to notice the attempt.
Also detects someone using Acting or a Vocation skill to impersonate or play a role (e.g. an assassin disguised as a servant).
Does not change behavior (that needs Influence or Trading), though understanding motives may hint how to motivate them.
Time Required: normally used while observing; no additional time. Studying an individual for at least an hour earns "Familiar with target".
Specializations: none required.
spell-lore:
Recognize spells cast against him, or written spells (recognition only; not a substitute for Runes). May give expected duration or area of effect of active spells.
Recognizing glyphs and symbols (if the character can detect them): difficulty increased by two levels.
Time Required: free action to recognize a spell and its parameters as it is cast, or to remember facts. If the spell is not in clear view, a Perception maneuver may be needed. Book research: an hour or more.
Specializations: normally Spells; alternatively Artifacts and other magic items.
Complementary Skills: knowledge of the spell list being cast from is complementary to recognizing or assessing that spell.
spell-trickery:
Reduces spellcasting penalties for hiding or modifying a spell's visual effect (if the visual spells optional rule is used) or hand and voice usage. See Spell Law section 4.2.
Time Required: part of the spellcasting maneuver (2-4 AP); no additional time.
Specializations: each specific spell list.
stage-magic:
Performing choreographed tricks, usually with props, from card tricks to large-scale tricks ("cutting" a person in half).
Time Required: duration of the performance. Preparation and rehearsal may reduce the difficulty.
Specializations: none required; optional: a type of trick (e.g. card tricks).
Complementary Skills: Trickery; Influence (to direct the audience) and Social Awareness (find helpful volunteers, predict their responses).
stalking:
Moving silently and unseen, using camouflage and shadows. Difficulty mainly from surroundings: easier in dark shadowy areas with lots of cover, harder in bright areas without cover; smooth surfaces and ambient noise make it easier not to be heard.
Opposed by Perception.
Time Required: normally part of movement. Pace penalties apply when moving faster than a creep (x1/2) pace.
Specializations: none required; optional: a specific environment (urban, forest, etc.).
Complementary Skills: Survival for the applicable environment.
stonecraft:
Extracting, dressing and working stone for building and decoration; ceramics count as artificial stone.
Time Required: highly variable (minutes to days). Creating items: see production times on the equipment lists. Assessing item quality: generally one minute.
Specializations: not normally required; could include mason, stone dresser, sculptor, gem grinder, potter, glazer, etc.
subduing:
Capturing or incapacitating a foe without permanent harm incurs a subdual modifier (Table 2.1x), offset by this skill.
Subdual attacks deal half concussion hit damage and use the Subdual critical table instead of the normal critical type, maximum severity E. See Subdual, Core Law section 9.7.
Subdual attacks are not harmless: always a risk of death in a general melee. For friendly non-lethal competition, resolve as conflicting skills instead (absolute maneuver per bout, or percentage maneuver until a total value is reached).
Time Required: performed as an attack action (2-4 AP); no additional time.
Specializations: none required.
Alternate usage: deal Krush criticals in melee instead of Puncture or Slash criticals. Same modifiers, except Unfamiliar Anatomy does not apply.
survival:
Living in a specific hostile environment: locating potable water, foraging edible plants, catching small animals (gathering, fishing, hunting); awareness of dangerous weather; finding shelter and camp sites; starting fires; improvising clothing or equipment.
Urban specialization: gathering food and materials from discards and trash rather than nature; otherwise the same.
Also used for finding other natural items: magical herbs, animal lairs, wood suitable for crafts.
Time Required: providing food, water and shelter for one person at the listed difficulties takes 4 hours. Each additional person supplied in the same time increases the difficulty by one.
Specializations: Urban, alpine, oceans, underground, ice caps/polar deserts, tundra, boreal forests, desert/xeric shrubland, prairies and steppes, temperate forests, hot deserts, savannah/grassland, tropical forest, or a specific xeno-environment (different plane, alien world, etc.).
swimming:
Non-native swimmers: swimming Base Movement Rate = 1/4 of normal BMR, adjusted by pace as normal.
Armor and Encumbrance penalties are multiplied by three while swimming (before Maneuvering in Armor skill is applied).
Non-aquatic creatures generally need Concentration to keep position in the water while taking any other action, unless they can breathe underwater (e.g. by a spell).
Diving: successful dive = no damage; partial success halves the effective falling distance; failure = normal fall.
Fatigue checks normally every 6 rounds while swimming.
Holding breath:
• After taking a breath: 12 rounds (1 minute) plus or minus the Constitution bonus in rounds (minimum 1 round).
• Then each round an Absolute Maneuver with the Endurance modifier (Body Development skill bonus plus any racial Endurance modifier). Starts Easy (+20) and gets 1 difficulty harder each round.
• A successful Adrenal Focus maneuver adds +25 until the Body Development maneuver is failed.
• Without a chance to prepare (thrown in unexpectedly, sudden gas): hold breath for rounds equal to the Constitution bonus (minimum 1) before rolling every round.
• Failure: inhaling. Inhaling water: 1d10 hits per round, Stun[-50] until the lungs are cleared, and an Endurance roll each round.
Time Required: part of movement; no additional time, but Concentration is normally needed to hold position while taking another action.
Specializations: none required; optional: diving or swimming with assistance (e.g. fins).
Alternate usage: used for Dodging if attacked while swimming.
tracking:
Bonus for tracking maneuvers: read tracks and signs and follow trails (footprints, broken branches, crushed grass, hanging cloth...). Unlike Perception, looks for specific details of how beings affect their environment.
A marked trail is easier to track. Uncontrolled bleeding: +50 to track a bleeding foe, +100 if bleeding more than 5 points per round; other cases by GM judgment.
Obscuring your trail: opposed conflicting skill vs the tracker. E.g. a result of 120 makes it harder to track you (-20); 80 makes it easier (+20). Pace penalties are x2 when using Tracking to conceal your trail while moving.
Time Required: finding or studying tracks takes one round per -10 modifier, minimum one round. Following tracks is possible at a creep (1/2) pace; at higher speeds apply the pace penalty.
Specializations: none required; optional: a specific type of creature.
Complementary Skills: Creature Lore or Racial Lore for the track makers; Survival for the biome.
trade:
Vocations focused on a specific set of trade skills rather than clients or managing an enterprise: business (finding customers and suppliers, presenting goods), or working as part of a group or unit (how it is coordinated, giving and receiving orders).
Other skills often apply as Complementary (Farmer: Survival to predict weather for sowing/harvest; a craftsman needs a craft skill plus this skill for business knowledge). Some aspects need separate skills (Thief identifies marks and sells loot, but needs Stalking and Locks to be useful).
Vocation skills are a catch-all for minor occupational skills; they do not replace several other skills. Also useful when impersonating or persuading a member of the occupation.
Time Required: highly variable.
Specializations: Blacksmith, Carpenter, Farmer, Fence, Gambler, Herdsman, Hunter, Merchant, Miner, Pirate, Sailor, Scribe, Soldier, Thief, Tinker, Trapper, Weaver, etc.
trading:
Negotiating, haggling, striking bargains that work for both parties, if a deal is possible. Sometimes resolved as an opposed Absolute Maneuver.
Haggling: opposed Percentage Maneuver with the buyer as the active party. Final price = 200% minus the result, giving 50% to 200%.
Difficulty depends on how the offered deal looks to the target: safe and very favorable = easy; shortchanging the target or putting him in trouble or danger = harder or impossible.
Finding buyers/sellers and negotiating prices: see Treasure Law sections 4.2 and 4.3.
Covers any exchange: bribery, barter, favors for goods or services, often diplomacy. The outcome of a conflicting Trading maneuver gives a general idea of how valuable an offer must be for a deal.
Also used to find a buyer or seller of particular goods.
Time Required: a simple price negotiation a few rounds; finding a buyer/seller or an elaborate deal hours or days.
Specializations: none required; optional: a particular line of business (e.g. weaponry), bribery, diplomacy, etc.
Complementary Skills: any skill used to create or appraise the goods, or an appropriate Vocation.
transcendence:
Reduces spellcasting penalties from armor (Spell Law section 4.2). In summary:
• Channeling: -3x the encumbrance percentage of any metal armor worn, plus a penalty for a metal helm (if any).
• Essence: -4x the encumbrance percentage of any armor worn (metal and leather), plus a penalty for any helm.
• Mentalism: penalty only for helms.
Penalties are offset by the Transcendence skill bonus. Table 2.1z lists full suits and helms; for mixed or partial armor use the encumbrance percentage from Core Law Table 6-4 (or Treasure Law Table 2-2b for the optional more detailed values).
Time Required: none.
Specializations: none required; optionally a single spell list.
traps:
Setting up, maintaining or disarming devices meant to harm or capture whoever sets them off, or to raise an alarm. Special tools or circumstances may modify the complexity.
Elaborate traps increase the difficulty (anti-tamper triggers, well-concealed parts, useless decoy parts).
Can also assess a discovered trap and find ways to avoid it without disarming (may be more or less difficult than disarming, depending on the trigger).
Time Required to disable or disarm: Easy and Light 2 rounds, Medium 4, Hard 8, Very Hard 1 minute, Extremely Hard 2 minutes. Absolute Success takes half the time; each Partial Success requires another time increment. Setting up a trap takes the same time if already prepared (bells on a string, spring-loaded bear trap); otherwise it may take considerably more.
Specializations: none required; optional: a particular type of trap (e.g. rope snares).
Complementary Skills: appropriate Survival when trapping local animals; Racial Lore for traps made by a particular race.
trickery:
Sleight of hand and misdirection: cheating at cards or games of chance, picking pockets.
Time Required: a quick sleight of hand (any difficulty) takes 2-4 AP if no preparation is required. Producing an item requires preparing it in advance (e.g. hidden in a sleeve or pocket).
Specializations: none required; optional: shell games, cheating at cards, picking pockets.
Complementary Skills: Influence when misleading the target; Social Awareness to gauge the focus of their attention.
unarmed-ag:
Any type of unarmed attack, including natural attacks for creatures with suitable anatomy.
Wrestling can also be used to break free when grappled (Grapple, Core Law section 9.8).
Time Required: unarmed attacks are a 2-4 AP action.
Specializations (skill stat): Strikes (St), Sweeps & Throws (Ag), Wrestling (Ag), Beak (St), Bite (St), Claw (St), Horn (St), Ram (St), Stinger (Ag), or Trample (St).
unarmed-st:
Any type of unarmed attack, including natural attacks for creatures with suitable anatomy.
Wrestling can also be used to break free when grappled (Grapple, Core Law section 9.8).
Time Required: unarmed attacks are a 2-4 AP action.
Specializations (skill stat): Strikes (St), Sweeps & Throws (Ag), Wrestling (Ag), Beak (St), Bite (St), Claw (St), Horn (St), Ram (St), Stinger (Ag), or Trample (St).
weight-training:
Using muscles to best advantage with least chance of injury (grip, lifting, body positioning). Bonus for strength-based feats (Core Law section 5.2).
Time Required: lifting a very heavy object (150% or more) generally requires 2-4 AP.
Specializations: none required.
woodcraft:
Processing wood from trees into boards, beams and finished goods. Crafting superior items and costs: see Treasure Law.
Time Required: highly variable (minutes to days). Creating items: see production times on the equipment lists. Assessing item quality: generally one minute.
Specializations: not normally required; could include sawyer, carpenter, ship wright, cart wright, cooper, etc.
writing:
Written compositions to inform, teach, inspire or entertain; a skilled writer can imply rather than state, or sow confusion and doubt.
If the objective is to persuade the reader, Writing may be used in place of Influence.
Books granting skill bonuses, including writing them: see Books and Manuals in Chapter 8 Training.
Time Required: variable, from minutes (brief report) to weeks or months (novels, epics, comprehensive works).
Specializations: none required; optional: stories, historical writing, poetry, diplomatic documents, formal reports, etc.
Complementary Skills: Influence when the purpose is to persuade; any Lore skill for the subject matter; a Vocation skill for documents related to that vocation (e.g. filing reports).
